The card's entry symbol leisaac.tasks.pick_orange.direct.pick_orange_env:PickOrangeEnv was confirmed at source/leisaac/leisaac/tasks/pick_orange/direct/pick_orange_env.py:61; it is a concrete direct task (it implements _get_observations and _check_success), so the card's GymnasiumDriver helper fits the environment step/reset interface. The upstream environment is a vectorized Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim GPU environment: dependencies/IsaacLab is the declared submodule read at its gitlink 3c6e67bb5c7ada942a6d1884ab69338f57596f77, and source/leisaac/pyproject.toml:41 pins isaaclab[isaacsim,all]==2.3.0. It was never imported or run. The GymnasiumDriver sim path (gymnasium.make(env_id)) needs the installed and registered upstream package plus Isaac Sim and a GPU; it was not run, and the package declares only the fake backend. A live sim deployment must also import the installed leisaac package so that leisaac/__init__.py runs the task registration before gym.make; this driver does not do that itself and that path was not run.

The fake is an analytic F0 in-memory stand-in, not a recording and not the upstream simulator. It keeps the reset/step/close surface and the six-value Box action, but models no PhysX, contacts, actuators, sensors, rendering or domain randomization. It returns 4 x 4 x 3 RGB stand-ins for the real 640 x 480 x 3 front and wrist images; its start offsets, image pixels, ee_frame_state, joint velocities and per-orange subtask flags are placeholders marked in fake.py. terminated stays false because task success needs contacts the fake does not model. The upstream cfg-derived observation_space and the actual _get_observations structure differ (the latter is the 'policy' dict plus 'subtask_terms'); the fake declares and returns the actual structure, and the gap discloses it. The real array size and the other omissions are in the fake fidelity gaps. The action space is the upstream unbounded six-value Box, so the driver declares no Limit and invents none; SAFE-014 has nothing to probe. The only numeric input bound is the class's ticks 1..10000 (schema), and no site overlay is needed.

Warnings left and why: G1.SUBMODULE_SOURCE because facts cite the declared dependencies/IsaacLab submodule (read at the gitlink above); G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only buffers the seed for the next reset, it makes no native call); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x2 for action_space and observation_space, which come from the Gymnasium base outside the clone; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because the upstream action space is unbounded; G8.NO_UNIT x4 for ticks, action.values and both seed inputs (bridge-derived simulator inputs with no catalogue unit). There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only the catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. The clone at 24d3bcd3f1e4585740fc79921782c41617237812 was read only and stayed unmodified; no upstream code was copied and no hardware backend was run. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed.
